title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's revised rollout window and distinguishes it from the older roadmap target. The cited documentation supports the controls and general Teams events licensing, while feature-specific licensing and chat-control gaps are appropriately qualified.

claims.claim: Event group chat is the private coordination chat for organisers, co-organisers and presenters in an event or structured meeting.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to allow presenters outside the hosting tenant to participate in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.claim: The meeting or event must have Enable Green room turned on to use event group chat.

claims.quote: External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: External federated presenters can see earlier messages if the thread shows history.
claims.quote: That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The presenter's stored tenantId changes from the organiser's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.
claims.quote: The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft describes this as a new cross-tenant chat path between the organiser's tenant and external presenters.
claims.quote: We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Both tenants must allow external access for this cross-tenant chat path.
claims.quote: Both tenants must allow external access.

claims.claim: The notice says the change stores no new customer data.
claims.quote:
Does the change store new customer data?

- No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

claims.claim: Attendees do not use event group chat.
claims.quote: Event group chat (organizers, co-organizers, and presenters) | No control. | Can chat with presenters and co-organizers. Attendees don't use this chat during events.

claims.claim: Both the organisation setting and a user policy must allow external access for a user to use it.
claims.quote: For a user to use external access, both the organization setting and a user policy must allow it.

claims.claim: External access organisation settings and user policies are turned on by default.
claims.quote: Both the organization settings and user policies are turned on by default.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Organisation external access settings can override user external access policies.
claims.quote: Your organization's external access settings can override external access policies.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A custom policy's Allow or block external domains value takes precedence over organisation domain settings.
claims.quote: Custom policy assigned to user: The value for Allow or block external domains setting in the custom policy takes precedence over organization settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing organisation external access settings are at Teams admin center > Users > External access.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access.

claims.claim: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $true enables the tenant federation master switch.
claims.quote: When set to True (the default value) users will be potentially allowed to communicate with users from other domains.

claims.claim: Existing external access user policies are at Teams admin center > Users > External access > Policies > policy.
claims.quote:
1. In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access.
2. Select the Policies tab.
3. In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.

claims.claim: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $true enables federation access in the external access policy.
claims.quote:
External access policies are configured by using Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy cmdlet.
Allow or prevent meetings and chat with other Teams organizations and Skype for Business | -EnableFederationAccess

claims.claim: The default external access policy is displayed as Org-wide default settings.
claims.quote: In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Join verification is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Events policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list, select Yes verify accounts or No verification needed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires presenter identity verification before event join.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference does not yet list ExternalPresenterJoinVerification, although the join-verification how-to documents it.
claims.quote: Searched: ExternalPresenterJoinVerification in the fetched Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference; no match. Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification, which explicitly documents the parameter and EOTP command.

claims.where: controls[3]; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope: Default; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch for external presenters in event group chat is documented, and Learn lists no admin control over event group chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external presenter event group chat admin disable PowerShell licensing ExternalPresenterJoinVerification chat; "event group chat" "control". Opened plan-events (event group chat: "No control."), manage-event-chat and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy.

claims.claim: Learn's Teams events planning table lists no admin control over the green room.
claims.quote: Green room | No control. | Can choose if green room is used for an event.

claims.claim: The unified Teams admin center External Collaboration section includes the existing External access page.
claims.quote:
The External Collaboration section in the Teams Admin Center (TAC) left rail provides a unified location to manage all external collaboration settings.
External access: This is the existing page to manage configuration of federation and communication with external domains

claims.claim: The notice asks organisations wanting the functionality to ensure external user collaboration is enabled at Teams admin center > External collaboration.
claims.quote: If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Organisation external access settings can allow or block specified partner domains.
claims.quote: You can allow or block certain domains in order to define which organizations your organization trusts for external meetings and chat.

claims.claim: The AllowedDomains parameter configures the allowed domain list.
claims.quote: Domain objects (created by using the New-CsEdgeAllowList cmdlet or the New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains cmdlet) that represent the domains that users are allowed to communicate with.

claims.claim: The BlockedDomains parameter configures the blocked domain list.
claims.quote: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains $list

claims.claim: Domain-list configuration is documented as operations separate from the printed federation-enabling calls.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains $Null
Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowedDomains $Null

claims.claim: The documented presenter join-verification policy is not confirmed to govern group chat access.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "event group chat" "ExternalPresenterJoinVerification". Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification, plan-events, manage-event-chat and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; verification is described for event join, not group chat access.
